title.value: Increased heat waves with loss of irrigation in the United States

scope_reason: The paper uses a regional climate model to examine how loss of irrigation changes heat wave frequency, duration and intensity in the contiguous US.

scope_quote.evidence_text: In this study we investigated how loss of irrigation affects heat wave frequency, duration, and intensity across fifteen heat wave indices (HINs) using a regional climate model that incorporated dynamic crop growth.

claims.restatement: In the model, averaged across all 15 heat wave indices in the US, loss of irrigation increased heat wave frequency, duration and intensity by 0.70 events/year, 0.62 days/event and 0.24°C.

support_span.evidence_text: We performed two 10-year (2002-2011) simulations using WRF3.3-CLM4crop to evaluate irrigation effects on heat waves. One is a simulation without irrigation (hereafter referred to as CROP), and the other includes irrigation (hereafter referred to as CRO-PIRR).

evidence.evidence_text: On average across all 15 HINs in the US, loss of irrigation increased heat wave frequency, duration, and intensity by 0.70 events/year, 0.62 days/event, and 0.24°C.
